iFabric Hackathon: Team Plan and Status

As of 5 October 2026 · Team iFabric · Trustworthy AI and Data Governance Hackathon · branch team-ifabric-5th-oct

We are proving that three collaborating AI agents can be trusted: every decision explainable, every risk controlled, every claim independently verifiable. The AWS workshop modules are largely worked through and the ServiceNow integration is built and tested. No control is complete yet (0 of 3). Next: freeze the threshold register, then build controls 16, 7 and 9 end to end, the evidence pack and our dashboard.

Detailed evidence behind this plan lives in the repo: gap-list.md (11 gaps) and notes/platform-observations.md (63 verified platform findings, cited below as #N).

  • Ordinary S1/S3 runs use 25K to 50K tokens. The masterclass example cap (10,000) and the kit default (2,000) would breach every run, so the C16 cap must be set from these figures and justified before the freeze.

2. How we are judged

  • Levels, in order: L1 use case running on AWS with MoDaaS guardrails and a Nemotron model (required, or nothing is judged); L2 controls on, evidence in the audit ledger, ServiceNow Control Tower adds observability; L3 ServiceNow extends the chain of evidence.
  • Axis 1: how many of controls 7, 9, 16 are complete end to end. A half-built control counts as zero.
  • Axis 2 (decides the winner): live 2-minute test driven by the judge; architecture quality; evidence a stranger can verify; honesty about failures.
  • Axis 3 (bonus): extra controls, inline verdict while running, adversarial testing, a second enforcement point with nothing rewritten.
  • Scorecard: Technical Execution 30, Impact and Innovation 30, Challenge Fit 20, User Experience 20.
  • Loses marks: undated threshold or dated after the test, partial coverage, evidence only we can verify, a finding closed without a re-test, thresholds inside control code, a design that only works in the request path.

3. Architecture

The live path is already running on AWS. Our work sits beside it: collectors capture the platform's records, stateless evaluators compare them with a frozen, dated threshold register, and the results go to the evidence pack and, for breaches, to a named owner in ServiceNow. Red labels mark verified platform gaps that our controls and gap list must account for.

Where the evidence comes from

SourceWhat it holdsLimits we verified
Gateway pod log (kubectl logs)Per-call tokens, modaas.run_id, action id: the figure of record for C16Short-lived: lost on pod restart. We must copy it into raw/ continuously (#27)
/aws/modaas/gateway (CloudWatch)Durable gateway lines with trace id and token usageNo run id; join via trace id to /modaas/evidence (#27)
/modaas/evidencePolicy decisions with correlation id (60 of 60 records)Guardrail blocks and kill-switch refusals recorded as ALLOW (#35)
Audit ledger /records?cid=Agents' own intent, invocation and result records (JSONL)Written by the agents; trace ids differ from the run's (#21); no model, tokens or guardrail verdict (#20)
Runtime spans and X-Ray48 spans per run per agent; gateway traces in X-RaySpans contain prompts and customer records (#22)
AgentCore metricsLatency Average and Errors Sum per runtime per hour (C9)Hourly only; cannot be presented as one run's latency
CR status and approvalsApproval annotations per assetSelf-asserted, empty signature; EKS audit logging off (#12)

Enforcement points

Enforcement pointWhereWhat it can doVerified behaviour
EP1 Shared model gateway (modaas-agw)Every model call from every agentGuardrail, Cedar authorisation, count tokens, refuseOnly path to Bedrock (direct calls denied). Cedar keeps no state, so no per-run cap inline today
EP2 Human approval queue (ServiceNow)After evaluation, off the pathAlert named owner, record response or silenceLive test incident delivered and read back
EP3 Kill switch (spec.paused)Out of bandWithdraw a routeModels: 33 to 41 s on nano-9b, under 2 s on super-120b; tools about 1 s (#36)
Tool call (Cedar / ToolConfig)Each tool invocationAllow or deny a toolChecks the called tool's policy, not the caller's declaration: undeclared tools are allowed (#37)

Design rules we follow

  • One contract, four transports: evaluate() in the path, emit() asynchronous, callback() for late verdicts (ServiceNow), pull() on a schedule (CloudWatch, Control Tower).
  • The register is never in the request path; evaluators load a frozen version. No threshold numbers in control code.
  • Evaluators keep no state: same inputs and rule version always give the same verdict. starter/evaluate.py already implements C16 and is our starting point (#62).
  • Raw records are never edited; corrections are new files. The ledger never interprets, telemetry never judges.
  • ServiceNow is never in the agents' request path. A ServiceNow outage is an evidence gap, not an agent failure.
  • One verdict vocabulary everywhere: SATISFIED, BREACHED, INDETERMINATE (data missing), NOT_ASSESSED (out of scope or no traffic).
  • A guardrail block returns HTTP 200: checks assert on finish_reason and token counts, never on status alone (#7).

Decisions needed now

  • Agent changes before the baseline: creating agents or applying the S2 fix makes a new agent version. Do it before the register freeze and before collecting the C9 baseline, or the comparison is not fair.
  • C9 metric: the team handoff uses hourly AgentCore Latency Average and Errors Sum per runtime; the kit's register.yaml suggests disposition-match rate instead (#62). We follow the handoff. Judges may ask about a single run, so the answer shows the hour windows that run fell in, labelled as hourly. score-run.py cannot be the C9 measure (#19).
  • C16 inline or after the run: Cedar keeps no state it could count with (gap 8), so C16 is checked after the run unless we build a reserve-then-commit check at the gateway. Say so plainly.
  • ServiceNow setting: a global OAuth setting was enabled on the shared instance. Confirm with a mentor that this was allowed.

5. Our dashboard

One web page that reads the evidence pack offline, so nothing live can fail during judging. A judge picks a control and a run or time window and gets the verdict with the records behind it. Mock-up with example data (real run ids, illustrative verdicts until the register is frozen):

AreaWhat it showsData source
HeaderThe claim C-FM-01 and which judging levels are shownEvidence pack README
Control tiles (C16, C7, C9)Verdict in words, icon and colour; measured value vs limit; rule version and dateassessments/
Ask a control questionControl + run or time window -> verdict, same as the CLIQuery tool
Run explorerEvery record for one run in time order, joined by run id and trace idraw/ gateway, ledger, /modaas/evidence
Six auditor questionsEach answered, with partial answers marked and the gap that limits themCR approvals, policy lines, ledger, gap-list.md
Human loopIncident, owner, delivered, responded or silenceservicenow/ delivery log
Adversarial testsAttack and observed result, including failuresadversarial/
Gap listWhat we could not close and whygap-list.md
  • Build: a static page (HTML + JavaScript) that loads the pack's JSON files. No server, no live API calls.
  • Accessibility: verdicts never by colour alone; contrast at least 4.5:1; keyboard and screen-reader friendly; plain-language summaries; works on a phone; export to PDF.
  • Keep the command-line query tool as well: judges said "we type the question; you drive your tool".

6. Non-technical plan (70 of 100 points)

Our story: Something went through our AI system on Tuesday morning. Three AI agents handled a customer's broadband fault. A regulator asks what they did, whether they were allowed to, and who was told when something went wrong. Today that takes days of reading logs. With iFabric, anyone can answer it in under 2 minutes, from evidence they can check without us, including where the evidence stops.

Security, latency and impact

  • Security: show each attack and the observed result. Verified: no credential gets 403; prompt injection is blocked at 0 tokens; direct Bedrock call gets AccessDenied; kill switch withdraws the route. Verified as weaknesses: undeclared tools allowed, direct tool-backend access, write token exposure. Do not run a forged ledger write live: it would pollute the graded ledger; cite the source check instead (#10).
  • Latency: gateway p50/p95 from per-call records; detection-to-alert time from the delivery log; kill switch 33 to 41 s vs under 2 s depending on model; ServiceNow and evidence writes add no delay to agents.
  • Impact: time to answer an audit question, timed before (AWS console alone) and after (our tool); share of governed actions covered; overspend caught per run (the S2 loop is the headline example).
  • Regulation: EU AI Act Article 12 requires automatic logging for high-risk AI. Say our tool helps meet it, not that it makes anyone compliant.
  • Path to production: pilot (3 controls, 1 scenario) -> scale (inline gateway checks, run ids in the durable log, per-agent identity, pinned tool code) -> harden (record signing, retention, independent assurance).

8. Rules we must not break

  • Nemotron models only, through the governed gateway alias. Agents run only on AgentCore or in ServiceNow.
  • Name everything we create ifabric_... (shared Control Tower and ServiceNow instance).
  • Account-wide limits are 100 model requests per minute and 2.5M tokens per hour. One request per second per agent is already 180 a minute for three agents (#41), so run scenarios one at a time.
  • Back up code to git and evidence to the team S3 bucket as we go; the AWS account is deleted after the event.
  • No secrets in code, files, screenshots or chat. Run tools/workshop-local/scripts/pre-push-secret-scan.sh before every push. Never touch other teams' records or the protected namespaces.
  • No signing, hash chains or slide deck: out of scope.
